findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The doc claims the Keycloak Operator 'will fail' when the `rolling-updates` feature is disabled, but the diff contains no operator production code that reads or gates on Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES. Operators following the doc will believe the Operator enforces the feature flag, but the Operator silently proceeds without it; any failure they later hit will be misdiagnosed. The only operator-side change is the test Dockerfile, so the documented behavior is fabricated relative to this diff.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3 while the vacated value 4 is reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED, so pre-existing automation written against the old documented contract cannot distinguish 'recreate upgrade required' from 'feature disabled'. A script that checks exit code 4 for 'recreate upgrade required' (the value the previous release emitted) now interprets FEATURE_DISABLED as 'recreate upgrade required' and proceeds to shut down the deployment for an upgrade that was never assessed, with no error surfaced — the metadata/check exit codes are a public CLI contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc.

[ADVISORY] The template hardcodes `--features=rolling-updates` into every rendered `update-compatibility` invocation, making the flag impossible to omit and coupling all guide examples to a preview feature name that will change semantics when the feature is promoted or renamed. When the feature graduates out of preview, every rendered guide example carries a now-redundant (and eventually rejected) flag; users copying the commands onto a version where the feature key differs get a usage error from the docs' own snippets.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled covers only UpdateCompatibilityMetadata; the FEATURE_DISABLED path in UpdateCompatibilityCheck (the other exit-site added in this diff) is never exercised by any test. A regression in UpdateCompatibilityCheck's guard (e.g. wrong exit code or missing printError) would go undetected; the two hand-maintained guard blocks in the two commands already diverge by exactly this lack of shared coverage.

[ADVISORY] The custom image now unconditionally bakes `--features=rolling-updates` into the build, so every consumer of this image (including any CI or local workflow that shares it) runs with a preview feature enabled by default with no way to opt out short of editing the Dockerfile. Anyone reusing operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image for non-rolling-update testing gets a server built with an experimental preview feature enabled, changing behavior of unrelated operator integration runs that assumed a stock feature set.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3 with no test in the diff asserting the new exit code, and testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message, not the new FEATURE_DISABLED=4 code. Any caller scripting `update-compatibility check` against the previous release (or any external automation keyed on exit code 4 meaning 'recreate required') now sees 4 mean 'feature disabled' and 3 mean 'recreate', silently inverting its decision path; a regression in these constants would not be caught by any test in this diff since UpdateCommandDistTest only asserts messages (assertError/assertMessage), never exitCode() for the failure paths (testWrongVersions asserts text only).

[ADVISORY] The doc states 'the Keycloak Operator will fail' when rolling-updates is not enabled, but the diff contains no operator-side gating logic — no operator source file is touched that checks Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES or a deployment feature list before applying an update strategy. Operators following the guide will rely on a hard failure that this diff provides no code for; if the enforcement lives in a commit not present here, the doc and code are coupled across PRs and one of them ships alone, leaving users with an update strategy silently proceeding (or crashing elsewhere) on a build without the feature enabled.

[ADVISORY] UpgradeTest enables ROLLING_UPDATES in createInitialDeployment for every parameterized case, so no test in the diff exercises the update-strategy paths with the feature disabled, leaving the documented 'Operator will fail' behavior (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc) unverified. If the operator's enforcement of the flag is missing or throws an unhandled condition (e.g., a generic NPE instead of a clear status condition), no test in this diff would catch it; users who omit the feature spec get an undocumented failure mode.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing consumers that branch on exit code 4 for 'recreate upgrade required'. Any script, CI job, or operator logic written against the previous documented contract (exit 4 = recreate needed) now sees exit 3, and worse, scripts that treated nonzero-and-not-2 as 'recreate' now see the new FEATURE_DISABLED code 4 and interpret a disabled feature as a successful 'recreate upgrade required' verdict, triggering unnecessary shutdowns.

[ADVISORY] The doc claims the Operator will fail when 'rolling-updates' is disabled, but no operator-side guard for the feature flag exists anywhere in this diff — the claim is not traceable to any implementation. Operators following the doc assume a hard failure, but with no diff-added enforcement in the operator reconciliation loop, a Keycloak CR with an update strategy but a custom image built without --features=rolling-updates proceeds against a server whose update-compatibility CLI exits FEATURE_DISABLED (4), producing an undocumented failure path; the doc assert has no matching behavior or test in the change.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled guard is duplicated verbatim in UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata (and printFeatureDisabled lives in the shared base), so any future third update sub-command can be added without the guard and silently bypass it. The next contributor adding an update-compatibility subcommand copies the run() skeleton without the Profile check; the invariant 'all update commands require rolling-updates' is enforced per-site rather than in AbstractUpdatesCommand, so it degrades on the next change.

[ADVISORY] The diff modifies UpgradeTest to always enable the feature but adds no test covering the documented failure path (update strategy set with 'rolling-updates' disabled), leaving the new behavior in the diff's own scope untested. A regression in the operator's handling of a disabled rolling-updates feature (the exact scenario the docs now warn about) ships undetected; only the CLI-side guard has coverage (UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled).

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3, and 4 is repurposed to mean 'feature disabled', so any existing script, CI job, or operator integration that branches on exit code 4 to detect 'recreate upgrade required' now interprets that condition as a feature-disabled error and takes the wrong remediation path. An operator automation run before this change that exits 4 for 'recreate required' now exits 3; conversely exit 4 — which previously meant a deterministic recreate recommendation — now signals a configuration error. Out-of-tree consumers of the documented CLI contract (the update-compatibility.adoc exit-code table) branch on these ints without versioning, so upgrades across this boundary mis-route upgrade strategy decisions silently. The docs table is updated but the wire contract is not versioned, and any caller with a hardcoded 4 keeps compiling/running and behaves differently.

[ADVISORY] testMissingOptionOnSave now asserts assertNoMessage("Missing required argument") after enabling the feature, but no positive assertion replaced it, so the 'save metadata succeeds with feature enabled and required option' behavior is verified only implicitly via the later testCompatible test; the case where the feature is enabled but the option is missing remains green regardless of whether validation fires. A regression that stops enforcing the required --output option on the metadata subcommand (e.g. after the new feature gate early-returns or validation is reordered) keeps this test green, so CI passes while the CLI accepts an invalid invocation. Whoever refactors validateConfig()/run() ordering gets no signal.

[ADVISORY] The literal 'rolling-updates' feature key is hand-copied across four places in this diff — the Dockerfile, the docs template's CLI example (`--features=rolling-updates`), the asciidoc CAUTION blocks, and the test constant ENABLE_FEATURE — with no single source of truth tying them to Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES. When the feature graduates from PREVIEW to default-enabled (or is renamed), the Dockerfile baked into the custom image keeps passing `--features=rolling-updates`; once the key is removed from Profile, `kc.sh build` fails and the operator test image stops building — or worse, the flag is silently accepted as a no-op and the gate tests stop exercising the disabled-feature path. The next editor must find and update four scattered copies.

[ADVISORY] The only operator-side coverage for the new feature gate is the happy path that pre-enables `rolling-updates` via FeatureSpec; there is no test in this diff that the operator actually fails (or refuses the CR) when update.spec.strategy is set without the feature, which is the behavior the new CAUTION in advanced-configuration.adoc promises. The documented failure mode ('Otherwise the Operator will fail') has no guard anywhere shown in this diff's operator source — only the CLI commands gate on the feature. If the operator reconciler is not separately updated in this PR, the doc advertises behavior that does not exist, and operators relying on the CAUTION to catch a missing feature get silent falling-through to the old update path instead.

[ADVISORY] The feature gate returns exit code 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED) which collides with what the documented exit-code table in update-compatibility.adoc previously documented as 'recreate required' semantics for consumers that cached the old mapping, and the failure is a hard command failure rather than a graceful degradation — an operator pipeline that runs update-compatibility as a pre-flight step gets no compatibility information at all when the feature is off. Automation invoked from an older deployment (feature not yet enabled) receives only the stderr message and exit 4 with no machine-readable result, so pre-flight tooling cannot distinguish 'feature disabled, enable and retry' from other errors without parsing prose. Consumers who branch on exit codes rather than output text get an unactionable failure.

[BUG] The public exit-code contract silently changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3, and 4 is reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED, renumbering an already-published API surface with no deprecation or documentation of the change. Any existing automation (operator scripts, CI pipelines, custom tooling) written against the previously accepted contract 'exit code 4 = recreate upgrade required' now misclassifies a feature-disabled failure as 'recreate upgrade required' (both exit 4) and a genuine recreate-required result as a success-adjacent code 3; scripts that branch on the old documented value 4 take the wrong remediation path (shutting down the deployment because a flag is off).

[ADVISORY] The feature gate runs before validateConfig, so a user with an invalid configuration now gets 'rolling-updates feature disabled' instead of the config error, changing the diagnostic behavior of an existing command without updating the existing guide's error documentation beyond a general caution. Operators debugging configuration problems through `kc update-compatibility metadata` are sent chasing a feature-flag issue first even when their real problem is a config error, and the error ordering change is not called out anywhere in the docs.

[ADVISORY] The RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was remapped from 4 to 3 in this diff, but testWrongVersions asserts only the error message and never asserts the process exit code, so the CLI's machine-consumable contract (which the operator and CI automation depend on) is completely unverified. A regression that returns the wrong exit code (e.g. FEATURE_DISABLED=4 instead of RECREATE=3, or a plain software-error 1) on the recreate-incompatible path passes the full test suite; any operator logic or user automation branching on exit code 3 silently breaks.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the printed error message and never asserts cliResult.exitCode() == CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), nor that no metadata/check output was produced. The new picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) contract added in UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata is unverified: a regression that prints the message but exits 0 (or exits with 1) passes this test, and downstream automation that distinguishes feature-disabled from a real compatibility verdict gets a false result.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled launches only the UpdateCompatibilityMetadata subcommand (@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME})), so the new feature-disabled early-return branch added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java lines 46-50) is never triggered by any test in this diff. The feature-disabled branch in UpdateCompatibilityCheck is exercised only via the metadata command's identical copy; if the check command's guard is removed or its exit code diverges (e.g. falls through to readServerInfo and throws), no test fails — the check subcommand's disabled path ships unverified.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently renumbered from 4 to 3, breaking any existing automation keyed to the old value. Any script, CI pipeline, or operator wrapper that already branches on exit code 4 to mean 'recreate upgrade required' now sees 3, misclassifying the result; conversely code 4 now means 'feature disabled', so a tool that interprets 4 as recreate will silently treat a disabled-feature failure as an actionable recreate recommendation. This is a breaking change to the documented CLI contract shipped in the same release with no compatibility note in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled check runs before validateConfig(), so misconfiguration errors are masked by the feature-disabled message and the check always returns FEATURE_DISABLED (4) for operators who follow the shipped docs without the flag. Operators upgrading from a prior version where update-compatibility worked without --features=rolling-updates get exit code 4 (which in the old numbering meant 'recreate required') with no prior guidance other than a preview-stage doc caution; combined with the exit-code renumbering, a disabled-feature failure is indistinguishable from the old recreate signal for anyone with existing automation.

[ADVISORY] The exit-code contract is silently renumbered: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3 and 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, so any external automation or script already built against the existing distribution (where exit code 4 meant 'recreate upgrade required') now receives 3 and, worse, interprets the new feature-disabled exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required'. Operators running update-compatibility in pipelines keyed on exit code 4 from the previous release get misclassified results after upgrade: a feature-disabled run is treated as 'recreate required' (coincidentally similar action, masking the real config error) and a genuine recreate verdict returns 3 which older scripts treat as an unknown/error code — the check 'succeeds' in reporting while consumers mis-route. No migration note or mapping accompanies the change.

[ADVISORY] The diff makes the feature flag a hard prerequisite for the operator's update handling (per the CAUTION: 'the Operator will fail' without rolling-updates enabled) but the diff contains no code path that detects and reports this condition for already-deployed Keycloak CRs, so existing users with an update strategy set get an operator failure whose cause is undocumented in status. Users upgrading the operator (or the Keycloak image, since only the test Dockerfile-custom-image bakes in --features=rolling-updates) with an existing Keycloak CR that has spec.update set hit an operator failure on reconcile after upgrade; the failure mode they observe is the operator erroring on their CR, not a clear 'enable the rolling-updates preview feature' signal from the diff itself — only the docs warn them.
